hook.line: Sooner or later you will want to say where an idea, a custom or a problem comes from. Spanish has a small family of verbs for origins, and each one has its own flavour.
hook.es: El proyecto surgió de una conversación.
hook.en: The project came out of a conversation.

examples.es: El proyecto surgió de una conversación.
examples.en: The project came out of a conversation.

examples.es: Esta interpretación parte de un prejuicio.
examples.en: This interpretation starts from a prejudice.

examples.es: La Candelaria se remonta a la época colonial.
examples.en: La Candelaria dates back to the colonial era.

examples.es: El cacao es originario de América.
examples.en: Cocoa is native to the Americas.

examples.es: La idea de la panadería surgió de una conversación con Vale.
examples.en: The idea for the bakery came out of a conversation with Vale.

examples.es: La duda surgió de la falta de datos.
examples.en: The doubt arose from a lack of data.

rule:
Four ways to say where something comes from:
*Surgir de*: something appears out of something else (*surgió de una conversación*).
*Partir de*: an argument starts from an assumption.
*Remontarse a*: something dates back to a time.
*Ser originario de*: native to a place.

*Surgir* has no agent: things simply arise, and nobody "arises" them. To say who made it, use *crear* or *generar*. Note the small words: *de* for the source, *a* for the date.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the vocabulary of origin. *Remontarse* is reflexive, so its endings come with *se*.

readAndPick.es: El proyecto surgió de una conversación.
options: The project led to a conversation.
The project came out of a conversation.
The project ended a conversation.

readAndPick.es: La costumbre se remonta a la época colonial.
options: The custom dates back to the colonial era.
The custom will last until the colonial era.
The custom was destroyed in the colonial era.

readAndPick.es: El cacao es originario de América.
options: Cocoa is travelling to the Americas.
Cocoa is sold in the Americas.
Cocoa is native to the Americas.

readAndPick.es: Esta interpretación parte de un prejuicio.
options: This interpretation starts from a prejudice.
This interpretation leaves a prejudice behind.
This interpretation causes a prejudice.

readAndPick.es: El problema surgió de un error.
options: The problem caused an error.
The problem arose from an error.
The problem fixed an error.

readAndPick.es: Mi familia es originaria de Medellín.
options: My family is moving to Medellín.
My family is visiting Medellín.
My family is originally from Medellín.

readAndPick.es: La duda surge de la falta de datos.
options: The doubt comes from a lack of data.
The doubt causes a lack of data.
The doubt is missing data.

readAndPick.es: El barrio se remonta a la época colonial.
options: The neighbourhood will return to the colonial era.
The neighbourhood dates back to the colonial era.
The neighbourhood was built after the colonial era.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *de* or *por* and type the whole sentence: *El proyecto surgió ___ una conversación.*
yourTurn.answer: El proyecto surgió de una conversación.
yourTurn.why: The source of something that surges comes after *de*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The idea for the bakery came out of a conversation with Vale.
yourTurn.answer: La idea de la panadería surgió de una conversación con Vale.
yourTurn.why: *Surgió de* + the source; nobody is the agent.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: La Candelaria dates back to the colonial era.
yourTurn.answer: La Candelaria se remonta a la época colonial.
yourTurn.why: *Se remonta a* + a period of time.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Cocoa is native to the Americas.
yourTurn.answer: El cacao es originario de América.
yourTurn.why: *Ser originario de* + a place says where something is native to.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: This interpretation starts from a prejudice.
yourTurn.answer: Esta interpretación parte de un prejuicio.
yourTurn.why: *Parte de* names the assumption an argument starts from.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The doubt arose from a lack of data.
yourTurn.answer: La duda surgió de la falta de datos.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: My family is originally from Cartagena.
yourTurn.answer: Mi familia es originaria de Cartagena.

pitfalls.wrong: Mi familia es originaria en Cartagena.
pitfalls.right: Mi familia es originaria de Cartagena.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The place of origin comes after *de*, not *en*.

pitfalls.wrong: El proyecto fue surgido de una conversación.
pitfalls.right: El proyecto surgió de una conversación.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Surgir* has no passive: the project simply *surgió*.

pitfalls.wrong: La costumbre se remonta desde la época colonial.
pitfalls.right: La costumbre se remonta a la época colonial.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Remontarse* points back *a* a time; English "from" does not carry over.

personal: Say where something in your life comes from, such as a habit, a family tradition or an idea, using *surgió de*, *se remonta a* or *es originario de*.
